enhancement.detailedExplanation:
India Code rule for sections 10–12: Section 10 identifies when agreements become contracts, subject to free consent, competent parties, lawful consideration and object, and absence of an express statutory voidness. Sections 11–12 regulate capacity and soundness of mind.

Definition: A contract under section 10 is an agreement satisfying the statutory conditions of enforceability, including competence, free consent and lawful consideration and object.

Ingredients / conditions:
1. There must be an agreement.
2. Parties must be competent under sections 11–12.
3. Consent must be free.
4. Consideration and object must be lawful.
5. The agreement must not be expressly declared void.
examples: Two competent adults freely agree to sell a lawful item for an agreed price; the section 10 conditions are satisfied unless another statutory rule makes the agreement void.
problemApplication: Apply sections 10–12: identify the precise statutory trigger, test each ingredient against the facts, consider the relevant exception or limitation, and state the statutory consequence.
keyTakeaways: Section 10 identifies when agreements become contracts, subject to free consent, competent parties, lawful consideration and object, and absence of an express statutory voidness. Sections 11–12 regulate capacity and soundness of mind.
A contract under section 10 is an agreement satisfying the statutory conditions of enforceability, including competence, free consent and lawful consideration and object.
